articleTitle: Power Quality Improvements in a Zeta Converter for Brushless DC Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: These paper delves into the precise control of a Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor across all four quadrants comprising forward and reverse motoring as well as braking leveraging a bidirectional DC-DC converter. This converter interfaces between the motor and a three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI), facilitating motor operation. In motoring mode, the converter orchestrates buck operation, drawing power from the battery, while regenerative mode sees mechanical energy transformed into electrical energy, subsequently stored in the same rechargeable battery via boost operation. The proposed scheme capitalizes on the frequent start/stop nature of electric vehicles, advocating for energy recovery with every braking event through regenerative braking. Furthermore, when an electric vehicle traverses downhill, controlled speed regulation enables the efficient return of energy to the battery. The utilization of MATLAB/Simulink software validates the seamless execution of these operations, ensuring optimal performance and energy management. This innovative approach offers a robust solution for enhancing energy efficiency and extending the range of electric vehicles, bolstering their viability in sustainable transportation ecosystems.

articleTitle: Flight Path Planning for UAVs Using Guided RRT* Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Flight planning is an essential pre-flight procedure that ensures the successful execution of mission objectives for any aircraft, including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The flight planning procedure is inherently complex and must accommodate multiple variables that may affect mission success. To tackle the intricacies of UAV flight planning, an improved version of the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) algorithm is being proposed to enhance the efficiency and speed of pathfinding for UAV missions.

articleTitle: Accomplishing Power Flow with UPQC in Distributed Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The increasing integration of Distributed Generation (DG) into power networks has brought forth new challenges related to efficient power flow management and power quality. The Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) is a versatile device designed to address both voltage and current-related issues in DG systems. This paper explores the application of UPQC to optimize power flow within a DG system, ensuring smooth operation and enhanced reliability. Through comprehensive simulations, the study demonstrates how UPQC effectively manages power flow by compensating for voltage fluctuations, mitigating harmonics, and regulating reactive power, both in grid-connected and islanded modes. The results highlight UPQC's role in maintaining stable power flow while improving overall system efficiency, contributing to more resilient and balanced power distribution. By integrating UPQC, this research offers a robust solution to the challenges of power flow in DG systems, ensuring compliance with power quality standards and enhancing the performance of distributed energy resources.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Analysis on Facial Skin Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Skin Diseases can have cerebral goods in addition to medical bones, especially for those who have disfigurement or facial trauma. Since smart widgets are so extensively used, utmost people may readily take clinical filmland of their skin issues on their faces. In image processing, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated amazing performance, constantly outperforming mortal bents. Using clinical images, this study investigates different CNN algorithms for the bracket of six current skin conditions on the face rosacea, actinic keratosis, seborrheic keratosis, lupus erythematosus, rudimentary cell melanoma, and scaled cell melanoma. Xiangya- Derm was used to produce a dataset of 2656 facial prints that represented the forenamed skin conditions. In China, this is the largest clinical imaging dataset for skin conditions. Five extensively used network approaches for these complaint groups were compared. An independent dataset with the same conditions from several body locales was used to apply transfer literacy. Transfer literacy models demonstrated better average recall and perfection. In a test dataset conforming of 388 facial filmland, the bestmodel attained recalls of 92.9,89.2, and 84.3 for lupus erythematosus, rudimentary cell melanoma, and seborrheic keratosis, independently. Recall and perfection were on average 77.0 and 70.8, independently.

articleTitle: Implementation of 23 Level Asymmetrical Inverter for Motor Driver Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Presently Inverters are crucial for satisfying the growing electrical requirements in developing nations. Several countries are increasingly adopting alternative energy sources, such as solar and wind power, in response to the growing energy needs. India, a developing nation, provides financial aid to individuals for the installation of solar power systems in their homes. This provides us with more opportunities to develop innovative inverter layouts and approaches. This study introduces a single-phase 23-level asymmetrical inverter that is achieved by combining a 13-level inverter design in a cascading manner. This study provides a comprehensive examination of the structure and configuration of the topology, with the objective of minimizing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). A 23-level inverter is implemented to handle both resistive and resistive-inductive loads. An analysis has been conducted to evaluate the feasibility of the simulation and hardware model findings.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Hybrid Electric Vehicle with PI/PID Using Quadratic Buck/Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: In recent years, as the focus shifts towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with international standards, automotive manufacturers have increasingly turned to innovative technologies, particularly fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs). Unlike traditional electric vehicles, fuel cell EVs utilize fuel stacks cell as its energy source, these FCEVs primarily fueled by hydrogen will emit only water and heat in the process Fuel cell EVs are recognized as zero-emission vehicles due to the lack of tailpipe pollutants. The proposed configuration includes an innovative setup comprising a fuel cell, electrolyser, and onboard PV cells. During periods of adequate solar irradiation, the PV cells supplement the fuel cell's power generation and additionally, during idle vehicle conditions, surplus power generated by PV can be converted to chemical energy via the electrolyser and stored as hydrogen in dedicated tank. To ensure compatibility with motor voltage requirements, a Quadratic bidirectional buck boost converter is employed. EV configuration proposed is examined by considering varying irradiance along with speed values by simulations conducted in MATLAB/SIMULINK. In this work Comparison of PI with PID controller topology is analyzed and the results have been presented for identifying the best suitable controller for the proposed configuration.

articleTitle: A Semi – Circular Patch Antenna with WiMAX Spectrum Rejection Properties for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: In this article, a unique band-notched ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna is described. It has a semi-circular radiating patch and an elliptical ground plane with a well-defined structure. A sharp band is eliminated from 3.4GHz-3.6GHz with a return loss greater than -6dB by exciting a ring-shaped slot on the radiating patch. The designed UWB antenna can operate at the frequencies ranging from 3GHz to 13GHz and a Bandwidth of 200MHz with center frequency 3.5GHz is eliminated at which WiMAX is assigned so as not to have interference with the users working at this band. Properties of the antenna such as Return Loss, VSWR, and Radiation Patterns for different parametric variations have been simulated in High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software.

articleTitle: Enhanced Eleven Level (EEL) MLI with Lower Number of Switches and Voltage Stress Applied to Agriculture Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: A single-phase, eleven-level asymmetrical inverter including three uneven DC sources, five bidirectional, and two unidirectional switches is recommended. Since it uses fewer switches to give more output voltage levels, the asymmetrical layout is recommended. Reducing THD without adding more switches or levels is the main objective of this endeavor. The best topology was found by conducting comparative analysis with earlier ones, and the load parameter design is described. Half height modulation and equal phase angle modulation are used as control strategies. A MATLAB/Simulink simulation of an EEL MLI asymmetrical inverter was performed. Here, several characteristics, In order to compare the THD obtained using the two methods, factors such as total standing voltage (TSV), cost function (CF), and power loss are investigated for both fundamental and developed EEL MLI.

Author Keywords: Total standing voltage(TSV) Insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT)

articleTitle: Solar Solutions: Outdoor Air Purifier Fighting Against Urban Pollution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Sun based open air discuss purifiers speak to an inventive and economical arrangement to combat discuss contamination by saddling renewable sun powered vitality for filtration forms. These gadgets utilize photovoltaic boards to create power from daylight, controlling progressed filtration and ionization instruments that viably evacuate poisons such as particulate matter, unstable natural compounds, and hurtful gasses from the air. Their flexibility and flexibility make them reasonable for different natural settings, whereas integration with shrewd checking frameworks improves operational productivity. By advancing cleaner discuss outside without producing nursery gas outflows, sun based open air discuss purifiers offer a promising pathway towards moderating the unfavorable impacts of discuss contamination on human wellbeing and the environment.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Urban Mobility - Comprehensive Predictive Modeling for Traffic Congestion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: In the rapidly changing landscape of urbanization, this study delves into traffic congestion management within smart cities. Leveraging a diverse dataset from Kaggle, which includes details such as timestamps, weather conditions, road types, and vehicle specifics, the research examines the temporal dynamics of congestion, identifying patterns across various times of the day, week, and year. By applying machine learning models like Linear Regression, Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, SVR, K-Neighbors Regressor, and MLP Regressor, the study evaluates their predictive performance, with a focus on distinctions in effectiveness using Mean Squared Error as a metric. The findings highlight the critical role of historical data and weather factors in accurate congestion forecasting, offering valuable insights for the development of smart cities. This research enhances the understanding of urban mobility challenges and provides a practical framework for implementing proactive traffic management strategies in increasingly complex urban environments.

articleTitle: ANSYS Maxwell Simulation for a 2 kW BLDC Motor Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The drive for sustainable development and green technologies is revolutionizing the electric vehicle (EV) industry, especially in crafting high-performance, eco-friendly solutions for transportation. Developing Electric vehicles industry has created a demand for high-performance systems. BLDC motors convert more electrical energy into mechanical power with minimal losses, reducing overall energy consumption and lowering en-vironmental impact. These motors eliminates harmful emissions, such as carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, contributing to cleaner air and a reduction in global warming. Our research mainly focuses on the performance of the design, applications of BLDC motor in the view of urban electric mobility. We have designed a BLDC motor which is specifically designed to use in EVs,with a capacity of 2kW and a rated speed of 3000 rpm, aiming to contribute to the advancement of electric vehicles. The main aim of designing motor is to create a highly efficient solution for two-wheeler electric vehicles, enabling them to carry up to three passengers while boosting energy efficiency, reliability, and sustainability in urban travel.

articleTitle: DevOps Practices Into Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: All industrial machine learning (ML) projects have their ultimate objective to quickly develop and deploy ML solutions. However, a lot of machine learning projects are failing, and never reach production. In order to address these concerns, this paper aims to investigate how manual ML processes can be automated and operationalised so that more ML concept can be put into production. The advantages of DevOps automation and machine learning capabilities are now being combined by industries. MLOps is the name of this combination. Our analysis found that while there are some similar aspects in defining MLOps, still there is a lack of standardisation in the term, which can occasionally lead to misunderstandings and uncertainty. We carried out the research, which includes a review of the literature and an evaluation of the MLOps tools, to fill this gap. These investigations have led us to define MLOps and identify unresolved issues in the field. In addition to this, we offer a workflow-based summary of all essential components. Finally, this paper gives guidance for applying DevOps practises to machine learning for researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: Interpretable Lightweight CNN for Colon and Lung Cancer Classification with LIME Based Explainability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Colon and lung cancers are one of the major reasons reported for cancer related death across the globe, which underscores the vital need for early and accurate method for its diagnosis. Our study presents a lightweight CNN model for classification of colon and lung cancer disease using histopathological images. The proposed model fuses Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) within adaptive residual blocks where skip connections are created by adding input tensor to the output of residual block, so as to enhance feature extraction and refine the feature map through inclusion of attention mechanism. Comprehensive evaluations on LC25000 dataset for both lung and colon cancers demonstrate the model's effectiveness in classification, with overall accuracy of 99.8%. In spite of its compact architecture with only 0.9M trainable parameters our model achieved high classification accuracy. Further to facilitate transparency and interpretability Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanation (LIME) is being generated which provides insights into the region which contributes to model's decision. The incorporation of LIME facilitates a deeper comprehension of the model's behavior, supporting its potential for clinical adoption and improving diagnostic reliability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Language Models Through Prompt Engineering - A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: In recent years, language models have undergone significant advancements with models like GPT-3, showcasing impressive abilities in natural language processing and generation. However, these models often experience from issues such as generating biased or unreliable content, producing inappropriate responses, or failing to fulfill specific user needs. To address these challenges, prompt engineering emerged as a promising approach by providing explicit guidance to language models. It refers to the process of designing and constructing effective prompts or instructions to guide language models like GPT-3 in generating desired outputs. In this article an attempt was made to address the role of prompt engineering, its techniques, and its potential impact on enhancing the performance and reliability of language models.

articleTitle: Portable Electric Tiller and Cutter Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Agriculture begins with human existence. It is an essential part of human life because it feeds us and manages the ecosystem at the same time. This is a very important point of view for living beings. But modern agricultural techniques are difficult and very intensive. Modern tractors that run on fuel are harmful to the environment and are not affordable for farmers. The main stage of farming is soil cultivation and traditional techniques are time-consuming and very intensive and modern ones are not cheap and damage the environment. The portable electric tilling machine uses a battery mechanism for machining with minimum cost, and processing time and increases productivity and efficiency with a healthy environment.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Applications in Disease Outbreak Detection Using Healthcare IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The Global Pandemic Early Warning System (GPEWS) represents a significant innovation in identifying and tracking disease outbreaks through the combination of data analysis and state-of-the-art machine learning technologies. This holistic approach utilizes sophisticated machine learning techniques to handle a variety of data sources, including historical outbreak records, real-time health data, environmental factors, and international travel information. By employing transfer learning, GPEWS can adapt pre-trained models to recognize both new and existing disease outbreaks, thereby improving its accuracy in detecting and monitoring emerging health threats. GPEWS gathers data from healthcare IoT devices to assess disease severity, categorizing cases into low, medium, and high-risk levels. This precise classification is essential for early detection and swift response to potential health crises. The system effectively addresses the issue of false positives and false negatives by using advanced algorithms that enhance precision and recall. The alert generation protocols are carefully designed to prevent unnecessary alarm while ensuring that genuine threats are promptly identified and reported to relevant authorities. Through the integration of these diverse components, GPEWS not only improves the detection of disease outbreaks but also enables real-time monitoring of their frequency and spread. The system's continuous adaptation to new data and its ability to refine predictions make it a vital tool in global health crisis management. GPEWS is set to transform pandemic preparedness by providing a dependable, real-time early warning system that equips health authorities to take proactive actions and mitigate the impact of disease outbreaks worldwide.

articleTitle: Cloud Based Load Balancer for Energy Conservation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Imbalanced electrical loads result in reduced efficiency of connected equipment and wiring, leading to substantial energy waste and financial losses. Maintaining equilibrium in the electrical system can be accomplished by evenly distributing single-phase loads across the three phases, either through manual or automatic methods. Real-time monitoring of voltage and current levels across all transformer phases and individual loads enables automated load distribution or management. This data can be instantly uploaded to cloud storage for remote accessibility, facilitating efficient load balancing and scheduling. A processing device executes an algorithm that analyzes the incoming data and determines how to redistribute loads across different phases based on the received current measurements. This process aims to bring the system closer to a balanced state. TRIAC Switches enable the transfer of loads from the current phase to any other phase. This system enhances efficiency and stability while minimizing time, energy, and financial losses.

articleTitle: Development of Enhanced Network Model for Image Dehazing Using Combined Transmission Map Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The elimination of haze from a single image presents a significant challenge due to its fundamentally ill-posed characteristics. Numerous prior-based and learning-based approaches have been introduced in the literature to address this issue, yielding visually pleasing outcomes. Most existing methods, however, presume a constant atmospheric light model and typically adhere to a two-step process: first, employing prior-based techniques to estimate the Transmission Map (TM), subsequently the computation of the dehazed image using a closed-form solution is carried out. This research relaxes the assumption of continuous atmospheric light and introduces a revolutionary unified single-image dehazing network that concurrently estimates the TM and executes dehazing. This novel approach offers a comprehensive learning framework, wherein the intrinsic TM and dehazed outcome are concurrently learned from the loss function. Comprehensive studies conducted on simulated and actual datasets featuring challenging hazy images concluded that the suggested method significantly outperforms existing techniques.

articleTitle: Multiport Bidirectional Converter with Resonant and PWM Modes for Drives Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multiport DC-DC converter topology specifically designed for drive applications. The proposed topology offers the flexibility to operate in reso-nant mode during forward operation, achieving both buck and boost modes by adjusting the switching frequency. A significant advantage of this converter is its bidirectional functionality, allowing seamless buck and boost conversions in reverse operation. Governed by control commands to wide bandgap (WBG) devices, this versatility highlights the converter's adaptability to various needs. Notably, the primary power source is a Fuel cell stack, with a secondary Source as LiFePO4 battery for storing regenerative power. The design of magnetics, control algorithms are essential for ensuring performance across all operational modes and suitable ratings up to several kilowatts, presents a major challenge that this work aims to address. The comprehensive range of modes and operational flexibility represent the most notable outcomes of this article, which is verified via detailed simulation results. The structure of the paper is organized as follows: Section 1 provides an introduction, setting the context for the study. Section 2 delves into the proposed topology and its various possible operating modes. Section 3 presents the modeling of the converter and discusses the various obtained plots, which is followed by the results and conclusion.

articleTitle: Smart Ignition Control and Accident Alert in Two-Wheelers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Motorcycle accidents often result in severe injuries or fatalities, a situation worsened by riders' non-compliance with helmet regulations and the delay in emergency response times. Addressing these critical challenges requires a comprehensive system that not only enforces helmet usage but also ensures swift action for helping the rider in the event of an accident. This work proposes developing a dual-function system designed to promote road safety and save lives. The system integrates advanced hardware and software components to monitor helmet usage in real time. Continuous surveillance detects when a rider is not wearing a helmet and sends alerts, ensuring compliance with safety regulations. Additionally, the system will be equipped to detect accidents, triggering an immediate notification to pre-defined emergency contacts. This rapid response capability is crucial in minimizing the time between an accident and the arrival of medical assistance, potentially reducing the severity of injuries and saving lives. By combining these functionalities, this initiative aims to create a safer riding environment, encouraging helmet use while providing a lifeline in emergencies. Ultimately, this system represents a significant step forward in motorcycle safety, with the potential to make roads safer for everyone.

articleTitle: RNN and CNN Based Ensemble Models for State-of-Health Prediction of Li-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Accurate prediction of the State-of-Health (SoH) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for optimizing performance and preventing failures in critical applications such as electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This paper presents an ensemble model integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), for enhanced SoH prediction. The ensemble approach leverages CNN's ability to capture spatial features and RNN's strength in handling temporal dependencies, providing a more comprehensive model for battery health monitoring. Using a NASA battery dataset, the proposed model outperforms traditional methods, achieving significant improvements in prediction accuracy, with up to 1.60% MAPE. This hybrid framework offers a promising solution for improving the reliability and efficiency of Battery Management Systems (BMS), enabling better decision-making for battery life cycle management. The results suggest that deep learning-based ensemble models can be a robust approach for SoH estimation, with potential applications across diverse industries.

articleTitle: Similarity of Depressive/Anti-Depressive Tweets with Happiness Index Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: People practiced social network use in recent days because of availability, technology and low-cost data availability. Approximately 200 billion tweets are being posted in each year, leads to consider that the tweets echo reflects the emotions of the people. Happiness Index derived from the World Happiness Report imitates a worldwide demand for more attention to happiness and well-being as criteria for government policy and therefore, its importance is increasing day by day. There is always a correlation between the social network posts and happiness/depressiveness and hence, the tweets from Twitter are considered for our study. Happiness Index is computed with several parameters and finding the dependency was not studied earlier. Three million tweets (depressive and anti-depressive) and information from the Happiness Index reports were studied and they exhibited a good coherence between “Social support and Freedom of life” with depressive tweets. Similar relationship was observed between Anti-depressive tweets with “GDP and Generosity”. Since the tweets are available continuously, the policy makers can study and get advantage from these tweets of an area before actually implanting any scheme for the people.

articleTitle: Demand Response Based Techno-Socio-Economic Improvements with Time-Varying Incentives at DN using Cuckoo Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The current energy crisis and the negative environmental effects of fossil fuel consumption have prompted a paradigm shift in favor of renewable energy sources. An efficient demand response (DR) scheme is proposed to shift the high load demand during peak load hours to the off-peak hours. High resistance to reactance ratio is a defining characteristic of distribution networks (DNs). With hourly shifting incentives, a price-load elasticity-based demand response method is presented to incentivize participants to redistribute their load utilization profile. This work shows how the combined effects of PV and DR can enhance the benefits of a radial distribution network in terms of technology, economy, and environment. The Cuckoo search algorithm (CSA) has been utilized to determine the optimal hourly PV power to be fed into an IEEE 22 bus test DN. Geographic equations are used to compute the installed capacity of photovoltaic systems (PV) in Jammu and Kashmir, India, while the beta distribution function is used to characterize the uncertainty of PV.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 31 Level MLI based Standalone PV system with Modified Incremental Conductance, Perturb and Observe Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: This paper presents a voltage regulator based on the perturb and observe (P&O) method, along with a capacitor compensator (CC) circuit, designed for a multi-level DC-link (MLDCL) inverter with 31 levels of asymmetric switch diodes. In order to achieve a constant DC voltage from PV panels for MLDCL in a standalone PV system, the P&O method is used to not only obtain the voltage but also provide maximum power at full load. The results show that P&O can generate stable DC voltages despite varying loads and environmental conditions due to its consistent 230 V output. Additionally, CC is employed to minimize voltage surges at the output when powering inductive loads. The IEEE 519 standard effectively gets rid of spikes and decreases the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the output voltage and current to below 5%. Instead of utilizing the perturb and observe technique for MPPT, a method called incremental conductance is being employed to decrease the settling times of the output voltages and environmental oscillations.

articleTitle: Design of Electric Drive-Train for Switched Reluctance Motor Based Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: This paper extensively examines the control aspects of fuel cell fed switched reluctance motor (SRM) used in fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEV). Integrating SRM in FCEVs presents several promising benefits, including improved efficiency, reduced weight, and heightened reliability. A boost converter is devised to merge the fuel cell output with SRM's asymmetric converter, after which the entire system underwent analysis to validate its effectiveness for FCEV. Utilizing advanced simulation techniques, the dynamic behavior of the SRM-FCEV system across various operating conditions is scrutinized, and efficiency, torque output, and transient response are assessed. Moreover, tailored control strategies are developed to leverage the unique characteristics of SRMs with a focus on achieving superior speed regulation, torque control, and energy management. The SRM is effectively controlled by employing the current hysteresis control technique to meet the variable speed requirement of the vehicle load.

articleTitle: A Short Survey of Truncated Multipliers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: As the world of digitalization continues to advance, extensive research has led to significant developments in the use of truncated multipliers. While traditional full-width multipliers were used in all applications, there are specific cases where truncated multipliers were adopted, albeit with some loss of accuracy. This shift sparked considerable research in the field. Truncation focuses on only considering the carries generated during the final result calculation, ignoring the least significant columns of the full-width multiplier. Over the years, numerous studies have explored ways to reduce circuitry by truncating the least significant bits (LSB) using combinations of AND and OR gates, all while aiming to minimize errors, reduce delays, and cut down power consumption. This study provides a detailed analysis of research on Baugh-Wooley architecture-based truncated multipliers from 1973 to 2024, offering a comprehensive review of decades of efforts to create smaller, more efficient multipliers.

articleTitle: Crash Shield: An Advanced Airbag System for Enhanced Bike Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Implementing airbags on bikes to enhance rider safety during accidents is a compelling idea. Our proposed system aims to prevent fall-related injuries, tailored for both bike racing and everyday motorcycle use, as well as elderly riders prone to falls. It utilizes an airbag that deploys upon detecting critical signals from acceleration, ground inclination, and obstacle proximity serving as an early warning and protective measure. For instance, if the MPU6050 sensor detects an angle of 45 degrees or less, or bumper switch ON then indicating an impending fall, the air compressor activates to inflate the airbag housed within the rider's jacket. Similarly, the system triggers inflation if the ultrasonic sensor detects obstacles within 3cm, further safeguarding the rider from impact. This integrated approach ensures comprehensive rider safety through advanced sensor technology and responsive airbag deployment. The system comprises essential components like power supply, microcontroller, sensors, airbag mechanisms, and dedicated circuits, effectively collecting and processing data to swiftly respond to potential falls and mitigate injury risks.

articleTitle: Emerging Technologies in Battery Management System for Next-Generation Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: Significant developments in Battery Management Systems (BMS) are required to improve performance, safety, and longevity of EVs due to their rapid evolution. The next wave of electric mobility is being shaped by new BMS technologies, which are the subject of this study. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning algorithms are integrated for precise condition estimation, predictive maintenance, and real-time adaptive control of battery parameters are among the key advancements. To solve the thermal problems of high-energy-density batteries, advanced thermal management approaches are presented, including phase transition materials and liquid cooling. The advancement of cloud-based and decentralized BMS designs allows for improved remote monitoring, scalability, and reliability. Furthermore, new opportunities and problems for BMS design arise with the use of solid-state batteries and multi-chemistry battery packs, notably in terms of maximizing safety and energy efficiency. As vehicle connections grow, the report also looks at cybersecurity's role in shielding BMS from possible attacks. Future BMS can greatly enhance the general effectiveness, safety, and ride quality of electric vehicles by incorporating this cutting-edge technology, opening the door to more intelligent and environmentally friendly transportation options.

articleTitle: Enhancing VANET Energy Efficiency with Gorilla Troops Optimization-Based Clustering and Routing: EACR-GTO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The mobile ad-hoc network, which is a component The Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET) is a wireless communication system that provides applications for navigation, safety, traffic management, and other areas with high-quality services. Because car sensors have a limited battery life, one of the main issues with VANETs is ensuring energy efficiency. To tackle this issue, we propose the Energy Aware Clustering and Routing (EACR) method using Gorilla Troops Optimization (GTO) to improve energy efficiency in VANETs. Initially, optimal Relay Nodes (RNs) are identified by optimizing the GTO based on factors such as residual energy, distances between sensors, distance between RNs and the Base Station (BS), node degree, and node centrality. Subsequently, energy and distance parameters are used to optimize multi-path routing with GTO. Additionally, Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) ensures efficient node scheduling during the transmission phase. As a result, EACR-GTO effectively minimizes energy expenditure, extending the network lifespan while ensuring reliable data delivery in VANETs. Experimental results show that EACR-GTO achieves improvements in Packet Delivery Ratio (3.33 %, 2.20%, 1.09%), energy efficiency (9.09%, 5.66%, 3.85%), throughput (5.26%, 2.56%, 1.01%), end-to-end delay reduction (7.69 %, 4%, 1.64 %), and a decrease in cluster packet overhead (11.76%, 6.25%, 3.23%) when compared to existing methods such as Multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO), Comprehensive Learning Particle Swarm Optimization (CL-PSO), and the Multi-objective Firefly approach.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT) in Smart Grid Technology and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as an industry-revolutionizing technology that has the potential to impact a wide range of businesses, including the energy sector. Integration of IoT into Smart Grid technology is among the most impactful and potential applications of IoT in the energy sector. The Smart Grid is a cutting-edge system for supplying power that makes use of real-time data, automation, and intelligent equipment to maximize energy production, distribution, and consumption. This paper mainly concentrates on the numerous ways in which the Internet of Things can be used in contemporary energy management systems, focusing on the important role it plays in boosting the functionality of Smart Grids. Communication between power generating sources, transmission networks, distribution systems, and end users is made possible through the integration of IoT-enabled devices and sensors in Smart Grid infrastructure. IoT aids in addressing the drawbacks of conventional power grids, such as wasteful energy utilization, a lack of adaptability, and a sensitivity to interruptions, by enabling real-time data interchange and decision-making.

articleTitle: Message from the Technical Program Committee Chair: ICISSGT 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Smart and Green Technologies (ICISSGT)
abstract: It gives us great pleasure to present the technical program of the 3rd International Conference on Innovations in Smart Systems and Green Technologies (ICISSGT 2024), organized by the IEEE Vizag Bay Section. As a biannual event, ICISSGT continues to serve as a prestigious platform for showcasing cutting-edge research and fostering meaningful discussions on intelligent systems and green technologies.
